raceIntelligence.headline: Antonelli Leaves Monza With a 66-Point Championship Lead
raceIntelligence.summary: A victory from 19th at the Italian Grand Prix turned a damage-limitation weekend into Antonelli's strongest championship statement yet. Madrid is the next test.

watchPoints.label: WATCH POINT 01
watchPoints.title: Antonelli's margin grows to 66
watchPoints.summary: The championship leader now has 267 points to Russell's 201 after converting a back-row start into victory at Monza.

watchPoints.label: WATCH POINT 02
watchPoints.title: Mercedes leaves Monza in control
watchPoints.summary: A one-two finish moved Mercedes to 468 constructor points and reinforced the team's advantage before Madrid.

watchPoints.label: WATCH POINT 03
watchPoints.title: Madrid becomes the next pressure test
watchPoints.summary: The new Madring round arrives Sep 11–13, giving the chasing group an immediate opportunity to respond to Antonelli's Monza gain.

articles.title: Antonelli Wins at Monza From 19th
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli charged from 19th to win his home Grand Prix, beating George Russell as Mercedes completed a one-two and the championship lead grew to 66 points.

articles.title: Antonelli Leads by 66 After Monza
articles.summary: The Italian Grand Prix strengthened Antonelli's title position: 267 points to Russell's 201, with Hamilton third on 191.

articles.title: Antonelli Now Has Momentum and Control
articles.summary: The championship leader leaves Monza with the strongest recent podium consistency and a 66-point advantage over Russell.

articles.title: Gasly's Shock Pole Set Up a Volatile Monza Grid
articles.summary: Pierre Gasly took pole in 1:21.786 ahead of Russell; Piastri's penalty reshaped the top six before the race.

articles.title: Antonelli Faces a Monza Recovery Race
articles.summary: The pre-race question was how far Antonelli could recover from the back. He ultimately converted 19th on the grid into victory.

articles.title: Monza: Why the Italian GP Is a Different Test
articles.summary: Low drag, heavy braking and slipstream management make Monza a uniquely revealing circuit.
